description: System definition for the node type taxonomy. Declares the 9 categories and the discipline of reducing every fact in Enki to one of them.

content.purpose: Everything in Enki is a node. The 9 categories defined in this pack are the only legal node types. Every signal, every extraction, every chronicle, every assessment must reduce to one of these or it cannot be stored.
content.principle: A small, stable taxonomy is more powerful than a large, growing one. New categories are added only through ceremony. Subtypes are added more freely (Tier 1 extension) but the 9 categories are sealed.

categories.purpose: Things that persist across time — people, organizations, vessels, aircraft, vehicles, facilities, accounts, devices, units
Locations — countries, regions, cities, points of interest, named operation areas, coordinate clusters
Discrete things that happened at a specific time — strikes, transactions, meetings, statements, sightings, earthquakes, weather alerts
Abstract subjects — conflicts, operations, treaties, technologies, ideologies — that signals are about but are neither actors nor places
Producers of signals — outlets, feeds, accounts, sensors, connectors, datasets, leaks. POV lives here, not on documents.
Discrete pieces of evidence — articles, images, videos, PDFs, audio, dataset rows, leak documents
Temporal anchors — daily, weekly, monthly, named period summaries. The long-term graph spine.
Epistemic statements — facts, observations, claims, hypotheses, questions, recommendations. Where contradictions live.
Emergent shapes that only exist because multiple signals form them — patterns of life, recurring meetings, supply routes, shell company chains, communication clusters

content.ldu_relationship: Every node, regardless of category, carries LDU lineage pointers (ldu_t_id, ldu_p_id) in its envelope governance block. This is how the system tracks which active set version a node was admitted under, enabling safe vocabulary evolution.
content.extensibility: Subtypes within a category can be added via Tier 1 extension. New top-level categories are forbidden in v1 — if a fact doesn't fit one of the 9, the right answer is to refine the existing categories, not invent a 10th.
